items.title: Section: Five Marks of a Field Vast Enough to Ripen Karma in This Very Life

items.zh: 復次，略由三因緣故，成現法受業。何等為三？一、田廣大故；二、思廣大故；三、相續清淨故。由五種相，田成廣大。一、從於一切有情第一利益安樂增上意樂住起，謂慈等至。二、從於一切有情第一將護他心住起，謂無諍等持。三、從第一寂靜涅槃樂相似聖住起，謂滅盡等至。四、已得一切不善不作律儀，謂預流果。五、極清淨相續究竟，謂阿羅漢及佛為首大苾芻僧。如是名為田廣大性。
items.en: Moreover, in brief, through three causes and conditions, karma comes to be experienced within this very life. What are the three? First, a vast field. Second, a vast intention. Third, purity of one's own continuity. Through five marks, a field becomes vast. First, rising from an abiding of superior aspiration towards the supreme benefit and ease of every being, namely the attainment of loving-kindness. Second, rising from an abiding that supremely guards every being's own mind, namely the concentration free of contention. Third, rising from a noble abiding resembling the supreme, still bliss of nirvana, namely the attainment of cessation. Fourth, one who has already attained the discipline of never committing any unwholesome deed, namely the fruit of stream-entry. Fifth, one whose continuity has reached the most thoroughly purified completion, namely an arhat, or the Buddha together with the great community of monks he leads. This is called the vastness of the field.

items.title: Section: A Weak Thread, a Trickle of Water, a Single Drop of Vinegar

items.zh: 若於是處，以深厚殷重清淨信心，捨清淨財，是名思廣大性。若前生中，於他所施衣服等物，由身語意不為障礙，亦不思量興染污心，以無有障障彼相續，當知是名相續清淨。若有於此三種因緣一切具足，當知彼業定現法受，亦於生受、亦於後受。若有與此相違三種因緣起不善業，當知亦成定現法受。或有所生一剎那業，唯現法受；或有所生一剎那業，亦現法受、亦於生受；或有所生一剎那業，三時皆受。譬如一縷其量微小，能持一華，一繫華已勢力便盡，不復能繫；復有一縷能持二華，再繫華已勢力便盡；復有一縷能持多華，多繫華已其力方盡。
items.en: Giving with a deep, earnest, pure faith, offering pure wealth, to beings who are suffering, impoverished, and without refuge, is called vast intention. Never having obstructed another's giving of clothing and the like in body, speech, or mind, and never having harboured a defiled thought regarding it, in a past life, leaving one's own continuity free of such obstruction, is called purity of one's own continuity. When these three causes and conditions are all complete, that karma is certain to be experienced in this present life, and also in the next life, and also in a later life. When these same three causes and conditions, reversed, give rise to unwholesome karma, this too becomes certain to be experienced in this present life. Some karma arisen in a single moment is experienced only in this present life; some is experienced both in this present life and the next; and some is experienced across all three times. Just as one thread, small in measure, can hold a single flower, its strength exhausted the moment it does, unable to hold more; another thread can hold two flowers, its strength exhausted only then; and another thread can hold many flowers, its strength exhausted only after holding so many.

items.zh: 又如流水其性微小，流經一步勢力便盡；有第二水其性稍大，流經兩步勢力方盡；有第三水其性廣大，流經多步勢力乃盡。又如酢滴其性淡薄，唯能酢彼一滴之水，不能酢多；有第二滴其性稍嚴，酢二滴水，不能酢多；有餘酢滴其性更嚴，乃至能酢眾多滴水。此中諸業差別道理，當知亦爾。

items.title: Section: How Bodhisattvas Sever Unwholesome Karma Without Severing Affliction

items.zh: 復次，十種不善業道唯欲界繫，亦唯能感欲界異熟，多於惡趣，少於善趣。又惡趣業，預流果時皆已斷盡。若諸異生世間離欲，或復生上，一切皆伏而未永斷。若不還果身猶住此，或復上生，及阿羅漢，諸不善業皆畢竟斷。若已證入清淨增上意樂地菩薩，一切不善業皆畢竟斷。此但由不忘念力所制持故，非由煩惱得離繫故。
items.en: Moreover, the ten unwholesome karma-paths are bound solely to the desire realm, and can bring about only desire-realm ripening results, more often in the evil destinies than in the wholesome ones. Karma bound for the evil destinies is entirely exhausted at the fruit of stream-entry. If ordinary beings become worldly free of desire, or are reborn into the higher realms, all such karma is only suppressed, not yet permanently severed. If a non-returner remains here or is reborn above, and an arhat, all unwholesome karma is permanently severed. If a bodhisattva has already entered the ground of pure, superior aspiration, all unwholesome karma is likewise permanently severed. This is achieved solely through the power of never losing mindfulness, not through affliction itself being severed and thereby freed from bondage.

items.title: Section: Karma Defilement's Own Closing Verse — And Rebirth Defilement Opens

items.zh: 殺生乃至綺語，亦業亦業道。貪、恚、邪見，業道非業。此諸業道餘決擇文，更不復現。後嗢拕南曰：自性相、廣、略、方便、與輕重、增減、及瑜伽、引果生、決擇。如是已說業道決擇。生雜染決擇，我今當說。如先所說生雜染義，當知此生略有十一。一、一向樂生，謂一分諸天。二、一向苦生，謂諸那落迦。三、苦樂雜生，謂一分諸天、人、鬼、傍生。四、不苦不樂生，謂一分諸天。
items.en: Killing down through idle chatter are both karma and karma-path. Greed, hatred, and wrong view are karma-path, not karma. No further deciding-discernment text on these karma-paths will appear. The closing verse says: self-nature in brief and detail, method and gravity, increase and association, drawn-forth fruit and decisive discernment. Thus the deciding discernment of karma-paths has been explained. The deciding discernment of rebirth defilement shall now be explained. As already explained regarding the meaning of rebirth defilement, it should be known that existence is, in brief, of eleven kinds. First, exclusively pleasant existence, belonging to a portion of the gods. Second, exclusively painful existence, belonging to the beings of hell. Third, mixed existence of pleasure and pain, belonging to a portion of gods, humans, spirits, and animals. Fourth, existence neither painful nor pleasant, belonging to a portion of the gods.

items.title: Section: Ten Kinds of Mastery, and a Bodhisattva's Journey Through Every Heaven

items.zh: 五、一向不清淨生，謂欲界異生。六、一向清淨生，謂已證得自在菩薩。七、清淨、不清淨生，謂色無色界異生。八、不清淨、清淨處生，謂在欲界般涅槃法、有暇處生。九、清淨、不清淨處生，謂生色無色界異生。十、不清淨、不清淨處生，謂生欲界異生不般涅槃法，設般涅槃法無暇處生。十一、清淨、清淨處生，謂生色無色界，非異生，諸有學者。
items.en: Fifth, exclusively impure existence, belonging to ordinary beings of the desire realm. Sixth, exclusively pure existence, belonging to a bodhisattva who has attained mastery. Seventh, pure-and-impure existence, belonging to ordinary beings of the form and formless realms. Eighth, impure-place-pure existence, belonging to one with the potential for final nirvana born in the desire realm in a place of leisure. Ninth, pure-place-impure existence, belonging to ordinary beings born in the form and formless realms. Tenth, impure-place-impure existence, belonging to ordinary beings of the desire realm without the potential for final nirvana, or, possessing it, born in a place without leisure. Eleventh, pure-place-pure existence, belonging to noble learners, not ordinary beings, born in the form and formless realms.

blocks.text: When karma ripens in this very life, three similes for its reach, and the opening of the last kind of defilement: rebirth.

Master Cháng Bǎi: with a vast field, an offering brings immediate result; the intention is earnest and complete. Offering to one just emerged from the attainment of cessation, a stillness like nirvāṇa, or from the absorption of loving-kindness, whose object is all beings, is such a field.

Master Cháng Bǎi: never having obstructed another's giving, one meets no obstacle to giving now. Giving with a hidden purpose is an obstacle. The weak thread stands for how many lives karma can continue. (Untranslated, 0636a12: similes of water flowing one step, two steps, or many; and a drop of vinegar souring one drop, two, or many: so karma differs in reach.)

Master Cháng Bǎi: at the first fruit, karma towards the lower realms is wholly exhausted; for ordinary beings it is only subdued. Bodhisattvas hold the mind by mindfulness of the teaching without severing every seed, so as to return to save beings.
Master Cháng Bǎi: affliction cannot act by itself, but reaches a path through volition. The meditation heavens: the first and second have joy and pleasure, the third pleasure throughout the body.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the desire realm is impure, yet one with pure potential, born where pure conditions can be met, is called pure. A noble one's place and mind are both pure.
The vinegar drop is a homely image: some deeds sour only themselves; others sour a whole cup.

quiz.q: What are the three conditions for karma experienced in this life?
options: a vast field, vast intention, and a pure continuum
much giving, strict ethics, and long meditation, by amount, unrelated to field or intention
vision, cultivation, no more training
faith, ethics, wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with a vast field, offering brings immediate result; the intention is earnest, vast, and complete; in a past life one did not obstruct others' giving, and so one's giving is pure before, during, and after. The next question takes up the English of the third.

quiz.q: The English has "unbroken purity." What is the problem?
options: 相續 is one's own continuum, not "unbroken"; §21's English itself says "one's own continuity"
no problem: 相續 means uninterrupted, a matter of sustained practice
"purity" should be "wealth"
"Third" should be "First"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: never having obstructed another's giving, one has no obstruction to giving in the present life. So 相續 is one's own stream of body and mind, free of such obstruction. "Unbroken" misreads it as duration, and is inconsistent with §21's own English.

quiz.q: The English has "the very first, stillest bliss of nirvana." What is the problem?
options: no problem: nirvāṇa is the first bliss experienced, the prior items being another word
the problem is "nirvana"
the problem is "noble"
第一 means supreme, not first in order; the prior items use "very finest," inconsistently
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the attainment of cessation is a stillness resembling nirvāṇa, where those of the third fruit and above abide. 第一 qualifies stillness as supreme. The same mistranslation appeared in fascicle 59 §§21–22, and here the English is inconsistent within one section.

quiz.q: What are the five marks of a vast field?
options: the rich, famous, elderly, learned, and kings, offerings to whom bring worldly return
father, mother, teacher, elder, friend
faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom
rising from loving-kindness, non-contention, cessation; stream-enterers; arhats and the Buddha's community
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: offering to one just emerged from the absorption of loving-kindness is a vast field, as its object is all beings; non-contention is an arhat's samādhi of protecting others' minds; the stream-enterer's precepts by nature make a special field. The timing "rising from" matters.

quiz.q: The English adds "to beings who are suffering, impoverished, and without refuge." What is the situation?
options: it is the treatise's own line, dropped from the Chinese, citable directly as the lecture says
the treatise has only 於是處; the English inserts the Sub-commentary's gloss, fitting the lecture yet not the text
a translator's flourish against the lecture
text miscopied from §25
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi follows the Sub-commentary: the recipients here are those suffering, poor, and without support. The content is thus sound, but the English has moved a commentary gloss into the translation without marking it, so it must not be quoted as treatise text.

quiz.q: Why does giving with an aim obstruct the purity of the continuum?
options: giving seeking something is an obstacle, blocking purity of the continuum
any giving is good, motive being unimportant
too much giving impoverishes
recipients are ungrateful
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: such giving with a purpose, seeking something, is an obstacle to giving and to the purity of one's continuum. This matches the treatise's "not harbouring a defiled thought." The English captures that phrase.

quiz.q: Can unwholesome karma also be certain in this life?
options: no: evil ripens only in hell, the present being for good results alone
only killing
yes: reversing the three, strong defiled volition also brings present results
only theft
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when in making evil karma strong greed, hatred, and delusion join volition, forming strong defiled volition, this too brings results in the present life. So the principle is symmetrical. The English "reversed" is fine.

quiz.q: What does the simile of the thread and flowers show?
options: single-moment karma may ripen in one, two, or all three times
thin threads break, evil karma soon ending
flowers outweigh threads
threads cost more than flowers
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the thread's strength stands for how many lives karma can continue. A single moment of karma may hold one, two, or many results. Two further similes in the source, water and vinegar, are missing from the English.

quiz.q: To which realm are the ten paths bound, and what do they bring?
options: all three realms, higher beings also killing, though less, ripening in all three
only the form realm
only the desire realm, only its ripening, more in evil destinies than good
unbound
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the ten evils mostly ripen in the hells, among ghosts and animals, and less among humans and gods. So bad results can also appear in good destinies, for example as a short life. The English is accurate.

quiz.q: When and how far are evil-destiny karma and a worldly-detached being's karma severed?
options: only arhats sever it, the first fruit still falling; birth above severs all, needing no path of seeing
at stream-entry it ends; for worldly-detached ordinary beings it is only suppressed
both at the path of seeing
both only at buddhahood
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: at the first fruit the karmic force to evil paths is wholly exhausted; for ordinary beings it is only temporarily subdued, not severed forever. A non-returner, as he adds, has severed desire-realm affliction though still living there. The English matches.

quiz.q: How does a bodhisattva's severing of unwholesome karma differ from a hearer's?
options: hearers sever seeds; bodhisattvas restrain by unforgetting mindfulness, seeds remaining, returning to save beings
bodhisattvas sever all as arhats do, hearers only suppressing, reversing the text as the lecture newly reads it
neither severs
bodhisattvas by ethics; hearers by giving
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas hold the mind by unforgetting mindfulness of the noble teaching, not severing all seeds, returning to save beings; hearers sever even the seeds. So the same result comes by different means. The English states this correctly.

quiz.q: What are "both karma and path" and "path but not karma"?
options: the mental three, and killing through chatter
all ten both
killing through idle chatter; covetousness, malice, wrong view
all ten path only
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: bodily and verbal paths are acts led by volition; affliction itself cannot act, yet achieves a path through volition, and so the three are path but not karma. The third member of the set, volition as karma but not path, is missing from the English. Note that the English "Greed, hatred" is used here.

quiz.q: The English has "drawn-forth fruit and decisive discernment." What is left out?
options: nothing: 生決擇 announces rebirth defilement, the verse having only six, the lecture's seventh being added
it omits 果
it omits 引
it omits 生, the poisons generating the ten paths; seven topics become six
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the sixth is the decision on what gives rise to karma defilement, three afflictions producing the ten unwholesome deeds, that is §§10–14. Without 生 the verse does not cover those sections. "Increase" also drops 減.

quiz.q: What are the first four of the eleven kinds of existence?
options: the three realms and the human world, by place
exclusively pleasant, exclusively painful, mixed, and neither
pure, impure, pure place, impure place
womb, egg, moisture, spontaneous
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first and second absorption heavens have joy and pleasure, the third pleasure throughout the body; the fourth absorption and the formless heavens are always of neither pain nor pleasure. The English "existence" for 生 is workable.

quiz.q: Who are exclusively impure and exclusively pure existence?
options: hell-beings; form-realm gods, by cleanliness of place, unrelated to ordinary beings or bodhisattvas
arhats; buddhas
desire-realm ordinary beings; bodhisattvas with mastery
animals; humans
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the desire-realm world is impure, and the bodies and minds of ordinary beings there too; a mastered bodhisattva abides in the signless without effort. The treatise then lists the mixed cases.

quiz.q: Why are ordinary beings of the higher realms "pure and impure"?
options: pure in body and impure in mind
sometimes in heaven and sometimes in hell
men pure and women impure
free of desire, pure; ordinary, with seeds, impure
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: form- and formless-realm beings have left desire, and so are pure; being still ordinary, with seeds unsevered, they are impure. 清淨 here has a narrow sense, freedom from desire. The English "pure-and-impure existence" follows.

quiz.q: What is impure-place pure existence, and how does it differ from the tenth?
options: the desire realm is impure, yet one with nirvāṇa potential is at leisure; the tenth lacks potential or leisure
rich homes are pure and poor impure, a matter of birth, unrelated to potential or leisure
both hells
both form realm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the desire realm is impure, yet one with pure potential born where pure conditions can be achieved is called pure; if born in the eight difficult states, even with seeds of the path, one cannot become pure in this life. The English is close.

quiz.q: Who has the eleventh, pure existence in a pure place?
options: arhats in the desire realm, any place being pure for them
noble learners, not ordinary, born in the form and formless realms
buddhas
wheel-turning monarchs
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the place is pure, free of desire, and the noble one's mind is also pure, without desire's seeds. The two purities therefore combine. The English "pure-place-pure" is a mechanical but accurate rendering.
